question.text: Scenario: Vikram Mehta, a CFA charterholder with 7 years of experience in wealth management at a private bank, wants to set up his own investment advisory firm. He plans to register as an individual Investment Adviser with SEBI under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013. His wife Neha is an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor who currently serves 50 clients. Vikram expects to start with 100 clients, charging an annual fee of Rs. 25,000 per client. One of his prospective clients, Mr. Rao, has assets worth Rs. 2 crore and wants both advisory and distribution services from the same family. Under SEBI IA Regulations, an individual Investment Adviser can serve a maximum of 300 clients and must apply for in-principle registration as a non-individual IA if clients exceed 300 or advisory fees collected during the financial year exceed Rs. 3 crore. A part-time Investment Adviser is limited to 75 clients. Accepted professional qualifications include CFA Charter, among others listed in the workbook. The IA must additionally hold a valid NISM Investment Adviser certification. Records of investment advice, rationale, and client interactions must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years. An annual compliance audit by a CA is mandatory. Importantly, a family member of an individual IA shall not provide distribution services to the client advised by the IA, ensuring segregation of advisory and distribution activities. Question 1 of 5: Does Vikram meet the qualification requirement to register as an individual Investment Adviser under SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013?

answer.text: Yes, because a CFA Charter is an accepted professional qualification under SEBI IA Regulations 2013
No, because only CA, CS, or CWA holders can register as Investment Advisers
No, because he needs a minimum of 10 years of experience in wealth management
Yes, but only if he additionally passes the AMFI registration exam

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, the workbook lists CFA Charter among the accepted professional qualifications for an individual IA. Vikram's CFA Charter satisfies the qualification requirement; the NISM Investment Adviser certification is a separate, additional requirement he must also hold. The Trap: Restricting eligibility to CA / CS / CWA only ignores the workbook's broader list, which includes CFA Charter. Inflating the experience requirement or substituting AMFI registration for the IA qualification is also unsupported. Note: The professional-qualification requirement and the NISM certification requirement operate together — meeting one does not waive the other.
